problems.title: Problem 9.12(a) — original

a. On April 1, Debtor pays Creditor $8,500 on outstanding debts. On April 15, Creditor ships $4,000 in goods to Debtor on Credit. On May 1, Debtor files bankruptcy.

b. On April 1, Creditor ships $4,000 in goods to Debtor on credit. On April 15, Debtor pays Creditor $8,500. On May 1, Debtor files bankruptcy.

problems.title: Problem 9.13(a) — original
problems.prompt: a. On April 1, Debtor purchased a new car, and gave Creditor a note for the purchase price, secured by a purchase money security interest in the car. Debtor took possession of the car immediately. Under state law, a purchase money security interest is deemed to have been perfected from the time the security interest was originally created (i.e., to “relate back”) if the appropriate documents are filed within 20 days of the debtor taking possession of the collateral. Creditor filed the necessary documents on April 25. On June 1, Debtor filed bankruptcy. Is Creditor's security interest in the car voidable as a preference? See § 547(c)(3), (c)(1), (e)(1)–(2).

problems.title: Problem 9.13(b) — original
problems.prompt:
Reference original part (a) facts:
On April 1, Debtor purchased a new car, and gave Creditor a note for the purchase price, secured by a purchase money security interest in the car. Debtor took possession of the car immediately. Under state law, a purchase money security interest is deemed to have been perfected from the time the security interest was originally created (i.e., to “relate back”) if the appropriate documents are filed within 20 days of the debtor taking possession of the collateral. Creditor filed the necessary documents on April 25. On June 1, Debtor filed bankruptcy. Is Creditor's security interest in the car voidable as a preference? See § 547(c)(3), (c)(1), (e)(1)–(2).

b. Same facts as in a., except the security interest is not “purchase money” — that is, the money loaned did not enable Debtor to purchase the car. Under state law, there is no grace period for perfecting a non-purchase money security interest; that is, for non-purchase money security interests, perfection is deemed to occur when the act necessary to perfect occurs, and there is no “relation back” to the time the security interest was created. Is Creditor's security interest in the car voidable as a preference?

problems.title: Problem 9.13(c) — original
problems.prompt:
Reference original part (a) facts:
On April 1, Debtor purchased a new car, and gave Creditor a note for the purchase price, secured by a purchase money security interest in the car. Debtor took possession of the car immediately. Under state law, a purchase money security interest is deemed to have been perfected from the time the security interest was originally created (i.e., to “relate back”) if the appropriate documents are filed within 20 days of the debtor taking possession of the collateral. Creditor filed the necessary documents on April 25. On June 1, Debtor filed bankruptcy. Is Creditor's security interest in the car voidable as a preference? See § 547(c)(3), (c)(1), (e)(1)–(2).

c. Same facts as in a., except (1) the state lien law gives the secured creditor 45 days to perfect, with relation-back effect, and (2) Creditor filed the necessary documents on day 35 (May 6). Is Creditor's security interest in the car voidable as a preference?

problems.title: Problem 9.14(a) — original
problems.prompt:
Creditor provided inventory financing for Debtor, and Creditor had a perfected security interest in all of Debtor's inventory, including after-acquired inventory. Debtor's inventory turned over about every 45 days. Debtor filed bankruptcy on June 30; 90 days before June 30 is April 1. All of Debtor's inventory on June 30 had been acquired since April 1. In the following situations, how much, if any, is the preference liability of Creditor? See § 547(c)(5) and (e)(3).

a. On April 1, Debtor owed Creditor $100,000, and on that date, the inventory subject to Creditor's perfected security interest was worth $100,000. On June 30, the debt was still $100,000 (no payments had been made), and the inventory was still worth $100,000.

problems.title: Problem 9.14(b) — original

In the following situations, how much, if any, is the preference liability of Creditor? See § 547(c)(5) and (e)(3).

b. On April 1, Debtor owed Creditor $100,000, and the inventory was worth $100,000. On June 30, the debt was still $100,000 (no payments had been made), and the inventory was worth $115,000.

problems.title: Problem 9.14(c) — original

problems.title: Problem 9.15(a) — original
problems.prompt:
Clem sold banjos on commission for Banjo Co., and as of May 1, was owed $25,000 in commissions. Clem also runs a shop, Banjo Fun, and purchased inventory from Banjo Co. As of May 1, Clem owed Banjo Co. $15,000 for the inventory. Assume that Banjo Co. does not have an Article 9 security interest in the inventory.

problems.prompt:

problems.title: Problem 9.15(g) — original
problems.prompt:
Clem sold banjos on commission for Banjo Co., and as of May 1, was owed $25,000 in commissions. Clem also runs a shop, Banjo Fun, and purchased inventory from Banjo Co. As of May 1, Clem owed Banjo Co. $15,000 for the inventory. Assume that Banjo Co. does not have an Article 9 security interest in the inventory.

g. Now assume that on June 28, Clem ordered and Banjo Co. delivered $5,000 worth of banjos on credit for a “4th of July” banjo sale (nothing says “corny Americana” like a banjo). Banjo Co. knew that the banjos were being delivered for resale, and gave Clem a one-year express warranty on the banjos. Banjo Co. filed chapter 11 on July 1. Unfortunately, about half of the banjos had a latent defect, causing the neck to snap off when used. In July and August, many of Clem's customers returned the defective banjos to Clem and got a refund from him. Clem, in turn, promptly notified Banjo Co. of the defect and his breach of warranty claim and demanded a full refund for all defective banjos. He also withheld payment for the June 28 delivery. When Banjo Co.'s Chapter 11 case later converted to chapter 7, the trustee sued Clem to recover $5,000 for the June 28 banjo shipment. What result?
